title: In Somnium Scipionis (Latin, Teubner ed. 1868)
author: Macrobius
description: Commentarii in Somnium Scipionis (Commentary on the Dream of Scipio) by Macrobius Ambrosius Theodosius (early fifth century CE), here in the Latin text of the Teubner edition by Franz Eyssenhardt (Leipzig, 1868), which also contains his Saturnalia. Macrobius comments on the 'Dream of Scipio' that closes Cicero's Republic, in which Scipio Africanus the Elder shows his grandson the cosmos from the Milky Way. The commentary became a principal channel of Neoplatonic thought to the Latin Middle Ages. It discusses the classification of dreams, the immortality and descent of the soul through the planetary spheres, the virtues, number symbolism (the monad, the seven and the eight), the structure of the cosmos and the planetary order, the music of the spheres, the zones of the earth and the antipodes, and the Great Year. It influenced Boethius, Chaucer, Dante and medieval cosmology.
